posts.title: The Altitude Problem: Why Strategy and Execution Were Never Separate
posts.description: Every post-mortem I have sat through has the same line in it. “The strategy was right, but execution let us down.” I have been pushing back on this for years. In 2013 I wrote Execution Rules, Strategy Drools, and my view hasn’t changed. There is no such thing as an awesome strategy with awful execution. posts.title: What Happens When Attacking Gets Cheaper Than Patching

posts.title: The Future of the Software Business
posts.description: When AI makes software cheaper to build and business processes easier to automate, who gets to keep the profits? For most of the last thirty years, software has been an extraordinary business. Build a product once, Sell it to thousands of customers, Charge recurring fees, Keep the incremental cost of serving another customer relatively low.
